beforeImage.name: WideOpenWest, Inc.
beforeImage.description: WideOpenWest, Inc. provides broadband internet, video, voice, and related connectivity services in the United States. It serves residential subscribers and businesses in its cable and fiber markets. The business is asset-heavy and recurring because it owns and upgrades last-mile broadband infrastructure and earns subscription revenue from network users. Company materials emphasize network reliability and broadband services, while public sources reviewed do not disclose the current revenue figure in the sources used for this batch. DigitalBridge and Crestview announced a take-private acquisition in August 2025 and completed the transaction in December 2025.

afterImage.name: WideOpenWest, Inc.
afterImage.description: WideOpenWest, Inc. (WOW!) is a U.S. broadband network operator providing high-speed internet, video, voice, mobile, business data and related connectivity services to residential, commercial and wholesale customers. The company operates across 19 markets in Michigan, Alabama, Tennessee, South Carolina, Georgia and Florida and reports nearly two million network passings. Operations began in 2001; the current corporation was formed in 2012 and adopted the WideOpenWest name in 2017. Crestview first invested in December 2015. DigitalBridge and Crestview completed a $1.5 billion take-private on December 31, 2025 through Bandit Parent and its subsidiaries; DigitalBridge Partners III holds approximately 63% and Crestview III approximately 37% of Bandit Parent's limited-partner interests, with equal general-partner control. InfraBridge is not a direct owner. SoftBank's signed acquisition of DigitalBridge remains an upstream manager transaction and was not treated as a direct WOW ownership transfer through August 19, 2026.
